title: Read often, kept close
sub: The fourth film of Data that moves, in Modern data basics: in 2015, a gene bank driven from Aleppo by war asks the seed vault on Svalbard for the copies it kept frozen there; at the university, how often each kind of data is read decides where it's kept, and the law and the business decide for how long: the cloud's storage tiers, named hot, cool, cold and archive, and old pay records moved to the archive tier after a year and deleted at seven.
howto: The film is drawn as the platform map up close: a dark navy night with lanes of light. Light blue is data moving and the platform, gold what people agree, green a check that passes, amber a person's turn, lilac with a lock what is personal. Where data is kept is shown as shelves, one for each storage tier: the hot tier at the top, close and quick to read; the archive tier deep below, frosted and still, cheap to keep and slow to bring back. The tools' pages are drawn for the film.
